question: For how many (not necessarily positive) integer values of \(n\) is the following value an integer? \[4000 \cdot \left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^n\]
solution:
Writing \(4000\) as prime powers lets us track exactly which factors could remain in a denominator. Since \(4000=32\cdot125=2^5\cdot5^3\),
\[
4000\left(\frac25\right)^n
=2^5\cdot5^3\cdot\frac{2^n}{5^n}
=2^{5+n}\cdot5^{3-n}.
\]
Because \(2\) and \(5\) are different primes, a negative exponent would leave an uncancelled prime factor in the denominator. Thus the expression is an integer exactly when
\[
5+n\ge0\qquad\text{and}\qquad3-n\ge0,
\]
or \(-5\le n\le3\).

Counting both endpoints, there are
\[
3-(-5)+1=\boxed{9}
\]
integer values of \(n\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
